text:
alex_ops: Heads-up — cluster hit soft-saturation again at 02:12 UTC, queue length spiked to 420 and we saw ~95% GPU util on p-rt-3. I opened a short proposal to change admission control from hard-reject to a degrade+queue approach. TL;DR: reject only when wait_time > 30s AND degrade (reduce max_tokens / lower priority / run smaller variant) otherwise. PR: https://git.internal/r/redwood/infra/pulls/482

maria_runtime: SGTM. can you paste the suggested policy config here?

alex_ops: sure, here's the snippet i put in the PR comment:

```yaml
admission_control:
  mode: hybrid
  max_queue: 1000
  max_wait_ms: 30000  # after this we return 503 (reject)
  degrade_rules:
    - when_gpu_util_gt: 85
      action: lower_model_size
      params: { target_variant: small-1, max_tokens: 128 }
    - when_queue_gt: 200
      action: throttle
      params: { concurrency_limit_per_key: 2 }
```

maria_runtime: nice, I like explicit max_wait. question: how do we surface degraded responses to callers so apps can opt-in to fallback behavior?

sam_oncall: cc @liz_product — product teams need a clear indicator in the api response (header/field) otherwise we're going to break clients. we should include something like `x-redwood-degraded: true` and a reason code.

liz_product: yup — need a deprecation plan. we'll roll to beta customers first. also want an endpoint to fetch current policy + capacity hints so SDKs can proactively change behavior.

raj_cost: cost angle — degrade to smaller variants buys throughput, but if we end up queuing a lot we could still blow monthly GPU hours. need to model cost per 1000 requests for each path (serve-small, degraded-late, rejected). i'll run numbers tomorrow.

olivia_sre: a few operational notes:
- We must make sure autoscaler cooldowns don't fight the admission rules. If admission allows lots of degraded small variants we'll see different sigs vs full.
- Need to add a circuit-breaker metric (admission_rejects_total / minute) to alert when rejects trending up.

alex_ops: good calls. i also want to add a backpressure header for clients so SDKs can back off and retry with jitter. Proposed header: `x-redwood-backpressure: queue=250;est_wait_ms=1200`. Thoughts?

maria_runtime: yes but keep it simple. est_wait_ms is helpful but noisy — only include when est_wait_ms > 200ms. otherwise just `x-redwood-backpressure: none`.

sam_oncall: from oncall perspective, prefer queue-first but bounded. hard rejects are easier to debug (503) but bad UX. degrade-first with short queue is the right default. Make sure the rollout has a fast kill switch to revert to current behavior.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: infra/admission/hybrid-v1 -> staging (started by alex_ops). build 2026-03-18-1753003000

olivia_sre: testing checklist for rollout:
- canary in us-west-2 with 2% of traffic
- synthetic load tests to validate wait time vs p95 latency
- ensure logs contain `admission_event:{type,reason,variant,queue_pos}` JSON for tracing

alex_ops: will add those to PR and schedule canary. i'm going to run an experiment now that forcibly sets degrade when util > 80 to see effect on p95 and queue length, will post results in ~30m.

maria_runtime: if experiment shows higher overall tokens served but lower cost, that's a win. if we increase tail latency for non-degraded requests, we need to rethink batching settings.

raj_cost: quick note — if degrade increases token churn because clients retry more often, cost could go up. need to instrument retry_count_by_reason.

alex_ops: agreed. adding metrics: `degraded_responses_total`, `degrade_retries_total`, `avg_wait_ms`, `rejects_total`.

sam_oncall: thanks. ping me when canary starts, i'll watch oncall dashboard and paging thresholds.

liz_product: can product engineering teams get a beta flag to opt into `x-redwood-degraded` semantics? i'd like to coordinate docs and SDK changes.

alex_ops: yes — adding feature flag `admission.hybrid.beta_clients = [org-123, org-789]` to rollout.

maria_runtime: small UX ask — add a reason code set like `degrade=size` or `degrade=queue` so we can classify regressions in evals.

olivia_sre: also think about region constraints — if a region is constrained we should prefer routing to compatible region variants before degrading. that should be part of smart routing policy.

alex_ops: noted. will add routing preference block to PR. thanks everyone, will post experiment logs in ~30m and update PR with checklist/rollback plan. :rocket:
